Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The players are already out in the middle now. Alyssa Healy and Phoebe Litchfield are the two openers for Australia Women. Renuka Singh to start proceedings with the ball. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Australia Women, in response, delivered an impeccable bowling and fielding performance. Their tight lines and timely breakthroughs restricted the Indian batters, with each bowler contributing to the collective effort. Now, as the players switch roles, Australia faces the task of chasing down 283 runs. The chase promises excitement, given Australia's formidable batting lineup filled with match-winners. India Women, on the other hand, will look to capitalize on the momentum gained from their batting display and strive to pick up early wickets. The stage is set for a thrilling second innings, where every run and wicket will play a crucial role in shaping the outcome of this pulsating encounter. Will Australia Women successfully chase down the target, or will India Women's bowlers turn the tide in their favor? The answers unfold in the upcoming innings, promising an exhilarating battle between the bat and ball.

Pooja Vastrakar says that, it was a very good innings for them. They planned to get 270+ on this pitch. She also stated that they aimed for 250 at the start but her team knew that they could go over 270 runs on board only if she and Jemi stayed on the pitch. They didn't target any opposing bowler but they tried to get important runs in each and every ball. Jemi motivated her by insisting on taking doubles. She also said that they got the target they wanted and hopes that they will defend it on the other innings. Ends up saying she is really happy with his personal batting against the Australian giants.

In the face of adversity, Jemimah Rodrigues emerged as the linchpin, crafting a magnificent innings of 82 runs off 77 balls, anchoring the middle order. Her partnership with Yastika Bhatia steadied the ship, laying the foundation for a respectable total. Pooja Vastrakar's unbeaten 62 runs in 46 balls, embellished with eight boundaries and two towering sixes, provided the late flourish India Women needed. Without the pivotal contributions from Jemimah and Pooja, crossing the 200-run mark would have been a daunting task. The Indian women showcased character and determination to post a challenging score of 282/8 in their allotted 50 overs, setting the stage for an intriguing second innings.

The first ODI of the enthralling three-match series between India Women and Australia Women witnessed a captivating first innings, unfolding a tale of resilience and individual brilliance. Winning the toss and opting to bat first, India Women posted a total of 282 in the end of 50 overs with the loss of 8 wickets. Early in the innings, the India Women batters faced the challenge of setting a competitive total against a formidable Australian bowling attack. With Smriti Mandhana absent, the onus was on Yastika Bhatia and Shafali Verma to provide a solid start. However, Shafali's early departure heightened the pressure. Richa Ghosh and Yashika forged a crucial 30-run partnership, but the fall of wickets at regular intervals, including the dismissals of captain Harmanpreet Kaur and Yastika Bhatia on 49, left India in a delicate position.
